analysis.title: US Power & Utilities: Midterm Election Outcomes: Impacts on Power & Utilities
key_insights: Democrats are on track for 54-56 US Senate seats and at least 228 House seats. BofA sees limited direct utility impact from the change in control, but the result could narrow the path for bipartisan permitting reform in the lame-duck session.

BofA says failure to advance the current permitting package would be negative for utilities. It would extend uncertainty around transmission, generation, pipelines and other infrastructure needed for accelerating power demand.

The Senate permitting bill would cut the statute of limitations for project challenges from as long as six years to 150 days, let projects proceed while agencies fix smaller deficiencies, and expand FERC backstop transmission siting authority. If the lame-duck window closes, a new Congress would restart talks under different committee leadership.
The large Democratic swing could increase anti-data-center rhetoric and calls for a national moratorium. BofA expects any such legislation would likely be vetoed by President Trump.

State results matter more than federal ones because governors, legislatures and utility commissions directly influence large-load policy, authorized returns, capital recovery and commission appointments.

Georgia is the clearest downside case. Democrat Keisha Lance Bottoms won the governorship and Democrats flipped the PSC from 3-2 Republican to 3-2 Democratic, so policy tone and direct regulatory oversight change at the same time for SO. Georgia Power's existing rate agreement gives near-term protection and SO could seek to extend the rate freeze through 2031, but its high equity ratio and allowed ROE could draw scrutiny.

Texas Democrat Gina Hinojosa won the governorship after calling for a formal data center moratorium and a special session. BofA sees added near-term uncertainty for SRE, CNP, AEP, ETR and VST, but legislative composition decides how much becomes law. The legislature could also revisit PUCT-approved transmission such as the 765-kV buildout.

Ohio Democrat Amy Acton supports a conditional moratorium until data centers cover 100% of utility costs. BofA lowers confidence in incremental Ohio data center upside for AEP and FE and underwrites their Ohio growth on reshoring, manufacturing and transmission instead.

Wisconsin Democrat David Crowley shifted late to support a pause during the state environmental review and to repeal the data center tax exemption. WEC, LNT and MGEE face slower customer commitments, and one of three PSC terms expires in March 2027.

Iowa (Sand, D) and Michigan (Benson, D) look more manageable. Their frameworks stress customer protections and formal rules, and BofA expects Michigan's pause to work as a bridge to final rules. BofA still views Iowa as an attractive large-load jurisdiction for LNT and keeps its CMS/DTE thesis intact.

Florida results are the clearest continuity case. Republican Byron Donalds won the governorship, avoiding Jolly's proposed ROE cap, and Republican James Uthmeier kept the Attorney General's office. BofA calls this modestly positive for NEE.

Pennsylvania's State Senate is 24-24 with 2 races uncalled. A Democratic Senate would give Governor Shapiro a trifecta and could revive a proposal linking allowed ROE to a 200 bp premium over the Treasury rate, raising legislative uncertainty for PPL, EXC and FE.

Arizona's Attorney General Mayes won reelection and Democrats lead two ACC seats, which would narrow the commission to 3-2 Republican. BofA treats this as an incremental risk for PNW and not a reset of its regulatory framework.

Kansas is close, with Democrat Holscher leading at 97.9% counted. She supports a statewide data center pause, but a likely Republican legislative supermajority and existing protections limit the practical effect. BofA stays relatively constructive on EVRG and sees KCC appointments, including a seat expiring March 2027, as the more durable consequence.

In California, a win by Insurance Commissioner candidate Jane Kim could push broader wildfire cost reform. BofA's own read-through is that this could be constructive for PCG and EIX longer term, though Kim has not proposed it.
Louisiana, North Dakota and Oklahoma Republican results preserve regulatory continuity for ETR, MDU, XEL and OGE. Montana PSC races are not final, and Republicans lead both.
Across jurisdictions, BofA names cost allocation, affordability, commission appointments and the conversion of proposed large loads into contracted projects as the critical investor variables.

market_movers.rationale: Greatest incremental risk because a Democratic governor and a flipped Democratic PSC arrive together in Georgia. Existing rate agreement and a possible freeze extension through 2031 give near-term protection.
Reduced confidence in Ohio data center upside after Acton's win and added Texas policy uncertainty. Ohio growth is underwritten on reshoring, manufacturing and transmission.
Lower confidence in incremental Ohio data center upside, plus Pennsylvania legislative uncertainty if Democrats win the State Senate.
Texas governor-elect Hinojosa's moratorium stance adds near-term policy uncertainty, though legislative composition decides the outcome.
Greater Texas policy uncertainty from the Hinojosa win.
Texas policy uncertainty is a risk, offset by Republican retention of the Louisiana PSC, which keeps focus on execution of Entergy Louisiana's investment agenda.
Texas policy uncertainty. The key distinction is between policies that restrict new connections and policies that shift cost and performance risk onto data center customers.
Crowley's pause and tax exemption repeal could slow customer commitments in Wisconsin. BofA still sees a substantial longer-term infrastructure opportunity.
Wisconsin pause risk, but Iowa's Sand framework is less negative than the party change suggests and Iowa remains an attractive large-load jurisdiction.
Slower customer commitments possible in Wisconsin. The question is delay versus a permanent cut to addressable load.
Donalds and Uthmeier wins avoid an ROE cap and a more adversarial Attorney General, which BofA calls modestly positive and the clearest Florida continuity scenario.
Mayes' win plus a possible 3-2 Republican ACC is a slightly less constructive Arizona outcome, but BofA views it as a change at the margin.
A Jane Kim win could force a broader debate on how wildfire losses are split among utilities, insurers and customers, potentially constructive but indirect and longer dated.
Same indirect, longer-dated wildfire reform read-through as PCG if Kim's lead holds.
Holscher's pause proposal creates headline risk, but a Republican supermajority and existing statutory protections limit it. BofA is relatively constructive.
Benson win largely preserves regulatory continuity and the expected data center pause is likely short lived.
Same Michigan continuity read as CMS. The MPSC term expiring July 2027 lets the Benson administration keep the commission's direction.
Montana PSC results are not final. Any Democratic win would shift focus toward affordability and large-load treatment but not change Republican control.
Same Montana PSC exposure as NWE, with attention on transaction-related commitments and large-load cost allocation.
Republican North Dakota PSC wins keep attention on company-specific proceedings instead of a change in commission direction.
North Dakota continuity reduces election-driven uncertainty but does not remove scrutiny of rate affordability.
Republican Brad Boles' OCC win preserves continuity, though approval of every generation or large-load filing is not guaranteed.
A Democratic Pennsylvania Senate could revive an ROE cap tied to Treasuries and make Harrisburg more important to the investment debate.
Same Pennsylvania legislative uncertainty as PPL if Democrats win the State Senate.

sector_views.rationale: Policy uncertainty rises around data centers, affordability and permitting. Impact depends on whether proposals become legislation, commission action or extended permitting delays, and risk is greatest where a new governor and new commission oversight coincide.

risk_factors: Lame-duck permitting reform could fail on calendar limits, political disagreements, election outcomes or resistance to transmission provisions.
State data center pauses or moratoria in Georgia, Ohio, Texas, Wisconsin, Michigan and possibly Kansas could slow large-load conversion.
Democratic-majority commissions or legislatures could target authorized ROE, equity ratios and cost allocation, as in Georgia and a possible Pennsylvania ROE cap.
Repeal of the Wisconsin data center tax exemption could hurt project economics even where construction remains legal.
Texas legislature could revisit PUCT-approved transmission investment such as the 765-kV buildout.
Commissioners could limit protections if projected loads fail to materialize, even under continued Republican control in Louisiana and Oklahoma.
Several races are not final, including the Arizona Corporation Commission, California Insurance Commissioner, Kansas Governor, Montana PSC and the Pennsylvania State Senate.

tension_points.bull_case: The Senate bill would shorten challenge windows to 150 days, let projects continue while agencies fix smaller deficiencies and expand FERC backstop transmission siting authority, materially improving development certainty.
tension_points.bear_case: Limited lame-duck calendar, political disagreements, election outcomes and resistance to transmission provisions narrow the path. A new Congress would restart talks under different committee leadership.
tension_points.what_invalidates: The lame-duck window closing without the negotiated package being accepted.

tension_points.bull_case: Georgia Power's existing rate agreement protects the near term, and extending the rate freeze through 2031 could address affordability while preserving investment visibility.
tension_points.bear_case: A Democratic governor and a Democratic PSC majority could scrutinize Georgia Power's high equity ratio and allowed ROE, large-load cost allocation and data-center-driven procurement.
tension_points.what_invalidates: The new PSC majority seeking structural changes to authorized returns, equity capitalization and cost allocation instead of accepting the rate freeze extension as customer protection.

tension_points.bull_case: The governor alone cannot set policy, and Republican legislative control limits how much of Hinojosa's agenda becomes law.
tension_points.bear_case: Hinojosa wants a moratorium and a special session, and a narrower Texas House majority could mean more negotiation on customer protections and a revisit of approved transmission.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Legislation that slows or restricts new connections, as opposed to policies that keep development going while shifting cost and performance risk to data center customers.

tension_points.bull_case: BofA sees a substantial longer-term infrastructure opportunity in Wisconsin.
tension_points.bear_case: Crowley's pause and tax exemption repeal could slow near-term development and hurt project economics.
tension_points.what_invalidates: The pause evolving from a narrow tie to the environmental study into a broader statutory or permitting restriction, which would turn delayed commitments into a permanent cut in addressable load.

tension_points.bull_case: Governing may moderate campaign proposals as affordability and the need to attract utility investment are considered, and narrow majorities could soften final bills.
tension_points.bear_case: A Democratic State Senate gives Shapiro a trifecta and could revive an ROE cap at 200 bp over Treasuries, which could materially affect utility economics.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Democrats winning the 2 uncalled State Senate races and the administration prioritizing the ROE cap ahead of affordability, data center or generation policy.

tension_points.bull_case: A likely Republican supermajority, HB2527 and existing customer agreements limit a gubernatorial pause, keeping BofA relatively constructive on EVRG.
tension_points.bear_case: Holscher supports a statewide pause, retains veto authority and gets KCC appointments, which could matter more than legislation.
tension_points.what_invalidates: The Kansas race result going to Masterson would remove the risk, while Holscher's appointment to the KCC seat expiring March 2027 is the more durable consequence.
